notes: Times in each capture are seconds from that capture's frame 0. A scene plays capture seconds [scene.trimSec, scene.trimSec + scene.durationSec].
Selectors were read from clients/discount-used-cars-site/src (Home.tsx, Layout.tsx) and checked on the running preview at 1440x900 and 390x797.
clock pins the page's wall clock to a Wednesday 2 PM in Houston, so the site shows 'Open Now' (it is computed from the time).

The phone capture is 390x797: under iOS's 47 pt status bar that makes the iPhone 14 screen, 390x844 pt, exactly (capturing 844 tall would stretch the phone or put the header under the Dynamic Island).

Part B (the sale desk) is inserted between shots 4 and 5: shot 4 ends held at 1.8x on the 'Admin · Staff Sign-In To The Sale Desk' row with the cursor resting on it, so part B can open on the click (same window, same 1440x900 viewport at DSF 2).
Shot 5 stops on the Trucks card: one more swipe reaches the lineup's fine print (finance terms), which is not in the on-screen fact list.

Shot 2 parks the real mouse in the left page gutter (x 64) while the cursor is hidden during the first scroll: otherwise the cursor carried over from shot 1 (342, 579) sits over the cards as they scroll past, and the Trucks card is already in its hover state (photo zoomed, white arrow) before the visible cursor reaches it.

Site content outside the on-screen fact list: shot 2 hides the lineup fine print ('15% down, 12.9% APR, 48 months') with visibility:hidden (layout and scroll targets unchanged). Shots 3 and 4 now hand off on the 'We Buy Cars, Too.' band, so the Discover tiles ('$205/mo', '4.8/5', '24 Google reviews') and the review quote never enter the frame and need no blur.
captureCss is injected into every shot: video-only brand fixes (see captureCss.why).

Shot 3's set-up click on the finder waits for the section's 0.9 s reveal transition (translateY 28 px): clicking mid-reveal put the cursor 4.7 px below where shot 2 ended. The typing ends 0.73 s before frame 0, so the caret is in the same blink phase as shot 2's last frame (56 frames after its last key).
Shot 4 repeats shot 3's last scroll in its preroll, then jiggles the mouse and hovers the same tile point, so frame 0 matches shot 3's last frame (tile hovered, cursor on it).

sfx.auto: From each capture's cursor.json (template shotCues): click → ios_tink −12 dB, 2 frames early; every typed character → one keystroke (key_1..7, sliced from macbook_keyboard) −18 dB ±1.5 dB, 1 frame early; every zoom-in → whoosh_short (rotating _lo/_hi pitch variants) −20 dB, placed so its peak (0.3 s in) lands just before the camera's fastest frame (zoom start + 9). All cues + masterDb (+10 dB).

partB.title: Discount Used Cars and Trucks: desk demo, part B (the sale desk)
notes: Part B (the sale desk). Same 1440x900 window at DSF 2 as part A; base http://localhost:5190 (the desk's dev server: the preview mock is off under NODE_ENV=production, so `next start` cannot run it; captureCss hides nextjs-portal, the dev indicator, checked in every frame).

Server: start-desk.sh (setsid, DESK_PREVIEW_MEMBER=fresh: a member with no name, no signature, onboarding not completed, NO temporary password, so onboarding opens on the name step). The mock's state lives in the server process: restart it before re-capturing 6 or 7.

Capture order on one fresh server (each shot's cursor starts where the previous capture ended): 6-desk-signin, 7-desk-onboard (this onboards Maria Lopez on camera; the same strokes are the member's saved signature for every later document), 8-desk-sale-start (before any walk-made deal exists; its css hides every row but Marcus Reed anyway), 9-desk-buyer, then the B4 set-up (sale.cjs with james-carter-to-registration.json → deal.txt) and 11-desk-guide --var deal=<that deal>, then 10-desk-readback (creates its own deal), then the off-camera complete sale (sale.cjs james-carter.json + ceremony-carter.cjs) and 12-desk-signed --var deal=<that deal>. Run 2 (2026-10-02): B4 set-up deal preview-deals-3, 10's deal preview-deals-4, off-camera deal preview-deals-5.

Every shot ends on the frame before its click's navigation (cutFrames / cutWhy on each shot), and the next shot opens on the new page with the cursor at the same point: 6→7 (sign-in → onboarding entrance), 7→8 (onboarding done → Handle A Sale), 8→9, 9→10, 10→11, 11→12 are jump-cuts in time on a click; 12 ends on Open / Print for the 130-U (the cut to B6). The camera at every cut is static (follow false) so it cannot jump: 1.5x focus 720,470 for 6→7→8; 1.4x focus 720,490 for 8→12.

Demo data: staff member Maria Lopez (fictional), buyer James Carter (fictional), 1418 Belrose Dr, Houston, TX 77034, Harris County, Texas licence 41927365, phone 713-555-0142, the mock lot's 2019 Toyota Camry SE (VIN 4T1B11HK5KU812345). No 'Example' and no '12345678' anywhere on screen: the sign-in email placeholder (you@example.com…) is hidden, the typed email and the nav identity handle are blurred, and shot 8 hides the six seeded 'Jordan Example' rows.

B6 (Remotion, not a capture): the off-camera deal's 130-U page 1 at 300 dpi is clients/discount-used-cars-demo/public/docs/130u-p1.png (2550x3300, from 130-U_Carter_812345.pdf); the bill of sale page 1 is public/docs/bill-of-sale-p1.png. Boxes (px in those PNGs, x0,y0,x1,y1): 130-U seller signature image 402,2871,890,2962 (ink 429,2873,~780,2962); printed name 'Discount Used Cars And Trucks, LLC (Maria Lopez)' 1227,2889,2139,2943; seller date 2163,2884,2382,2944; seller band (signature + printed name + date + labels) 392,2860,2392,2992. Money on the 130-U: box 38(a) '$ 3663.06' 1046,2243,1194,2299 (blur it if the page is shown legibly). Bill of sale money column 1800,2590,2390,3020 ($3,663.06 / $0.00 / $336.94 / $4,000.00).

Merged into the part A storyboard on 2026-10-02 (Compose v2). Each part B shot carries base http://localhost:5190 (capture.cjs: a shot's base wins over storyboard.base), its own clock and timezone, and partB.captureCss pasted into its css. storyboard.captureCss (part A's site fixes) is still prepended by capture.cjs; none of its selectors exist on the desk, so it changes no pixel.

Clock: 2026-10-02T14:00:00-05:00 (a Friday; the dealer is open Tue-Sat), the date the off-camera deal's documents were signed (the server's real date). Only 7-desk-onboard shows a client-side date (the pad's 'Signed: 10/02/2026'); it was re-captured with this clock. 6 and 8-12 were captured with 2026-10-01 and show no client-side date (12's 'Signed Oct 2, 2026' comes from the server).

Composition (clients/discount-used-cars-demo/src/demo/timeline.ts, Compose v2): heads trimmed 8 0.367 s, 9 0.167, 10 0.233, 11 0.233, 12 0.267 (zoomShift moves 8's pull-back and 12's push by the trim); cameras re-aimed with zoomFocus so no edge cuts text: 6/7/8-head 1.45x on 720,482; the sale steps 8-12 1.32x on 720,490; the read-back 2.0x on 720,472; the packet 1.62x on 720,356. B6 is DocScene (theme.doc, project.doc). Part B = 920 desk frames + 111 doc frames = 34.4 s; the film is 2508 frames (83.6 s).

captureCss.why: Video-only CSS for every part-B shot (the desk source is never edited): the Next.js dev indicator (nextjs-portal) is hidden; the two green #3F5A43 accents are drawn in ink (black and white brand); the nav's identity handle (the preview account's email) is blurred; the stray block after the sale head is hidden; the sign-in email field is a privacy blur (typed text transparent with a soft dark shadow) and its placeholder 'you@example.com or your handle' is hidden (no 'example' on screen); the onboarding signature step keeps its height so the pad does not jump.
